paragraphs.title: The Famine and Atonement to the Gibeonites

easy.explanation: The KJV says there was a famine for three years, year after year.
easy.q: How long did the famine last in the days of David?

easy.explanation: David inquired of the LORD, and the LORD answered him.
easy.q: Of whom did David inquire concerning the famine?

easy.explanation: The LORD said it was for Saul and his bloody house, because he slew the Gibeonites.
easy.q: Whom did the LORD say had caused the trouble against the Gibeonites?

answers: What he should do for them
medium.explanation: David asked, “What shall I do for you?” and how he could make atonement.
medium.q: What did David ask the Gibeonites after asking how to make atonement?

medium.explanation: They asked for seven men of Saul’s sons to be delivered to them.
medium.q: What did the Gibeonites request instead of silver or gold?

medium.explanation: David was asking how he could make amends and satisfy the Gibeonites concerning Saul’s offense.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “make the atonement” mean in this context?

answers: The famine caused Saul to attack Israel
The famine was connected with Saul’s killing of the Gibeonites
The famine was caused by the Gibeonites
challenge.explanation: The LORD connected the famine with Saul’s bloody offense against the Gibeonites.
challenge.q: What connection did the LORD make between the famine and Saul?

challenge.explanation: The passage says the children of Israel had sworn unto the Gibeonites.
challenge.q: Why did David have to deal with the Gibeonites’ complaint?

answers: They wanted a remedy connected to Saul’s offense
challenge.explanation: They rejected financial payment and requested a judgment concerning Saul’s house.
challenge.q: What does the Gibeonites’ refusal of silver and gold show?

paragraphs.title: The Executed Sons, Rizpah, and the Honor of the Dead

easy.explanation: David spared Mephibosheth because of the oath between David and Jonathan.
easy.q: Whom did the king spare from being delivered to the Gibeonites?

easy.explanation: Rizpah the daughter of Aiah spread sackcloth and guarded the bodies.
easy.q: Who guarded the bodies from the birds and beasts?

answers: In the sepulchre of Kish his father
easy.explanation: They were buried in the country of Benjamin, in Zelah, in the sepulchre of Kish.
easy.q: Where were the bones of Saul and Jonathan buried?

answers: Because of the LORD’s oath between David and Jonathan
medium.explanation: The KJV says David spared him because of the LORD’s oath between David and Jonathan.
David delivered seven men of Saul’s sons to the Gibeonites.
medium.q: How many men of Saul’s sons were delivered to the Gibeonites?

answers: Execute them by hanging as punishment
medium.explanation: The seven men were hanged before the LORD as the requested judgment.
medium.q: What did the Gibeonites mean by saying they would “hang them up”?

answers: Rizpah’s faithful guarding of the bodies
challenge.explanation: After David was told what Rizpah had done, he gathered the bones and arranged a proper burial.
challenge.q: What event prompted David to gather the bones of Saul, Jonathan, and the executed men?

answers: Burial, famine, execution, and then Rizpah’s watch
Rizpah’s watch, gathering and burial of the bones, and then God’s being entreated for the land
Battle with the Philistines, burial, and then the selection of seven men
challenge.explanation: Rizpah guarded the bodies; David gathered and buried the bones; afterward God was entreated for the land.
challenge.q: Which sequence of events best matches the passage?

answers: The Gibeonites demanded seven more men
God was entreated for the land
challenge.explanation: The passage concludes, “And after that God was intreated for the land.”
challenge.q: What happened after the king’s commands were carried out and the bones were buried?

paragraphs.title: David’s Wars Against the Descendants of Rapha

easy.explanation: The passage describes repeated wars with the Philistines.
easy.q: Against whom did David and his servants fight?

easy.explanation: Abishai succoured David and smote the Philistine who intended to kill him.
easy.q: Who helped David when he became faint?

easy.explanation: The final verse says, “These four were born to the giant in Gath, and fell.”
easy.q: How many descendants of the giant fell by David and his servants?

answers: They feared that he would quench the light of Israel
medium.explanation: They feared David’s death and told him not to quench the light of Israel.
medium.q: Why did David’s men swear that he should go no more to battle?

answers: Six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot
A spear weighing three hundred shekels
A new sword unlike any other
medium.explanation: He had six fingers on every hand and six toes on every foot, four and twenty in number.
medium.q: What unusual physical feature did one of the giant’s descendants have?

medium.explanation: The man openly challenged Israel, and Jonathan slew him.
medium.q: What does “he defied Israel” mean in this passage?

answers: Several powerful descendants of the giant fell in different battles
The descendants of the giant served in Israel’s army
challenge.explanation: The passage names four different descendants of the giant who fell in battle.
challenge.q: What can be concluded from the several battles involving descendants of the giant?

challenge.explanation: The final verse says they fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.
challenge.q: Who defeated the four descendants of the giant according to the summary?

answers: David was a central leader whose life was vital to Israel
David carried a torch in battle
David was responsible for lighting the camp
challenge.explanation: David was viewed as Israel’s essential leader, so his men feared his death.
challenge.q: What does the expression “the light of Israel” signify concerning David?
